newsitem.title: USA: Demand for machine tools fell in February.
newsitem.headline: Demand for machine tools fell in February.

text.p: Demand for U.S.-made machine tools fell slightly in February from the previous month, the American Machine Tool Distributors' Association and the Association for Manufacturing Technology said Sunday.
Total demand in February dipped 4 percent to an estimated $562 million from a revised $583 million in January. But it was up 22 percent from the $461 million estimate for February 1996.
The January estimate was revised down from $649 million reported a month ago.
Machine tools are used to shape metal in making everything from bicycles to aircraft. Demand for these tools provides a leading indicator of the pace of the nation's manufacturing sector.

By region, the joint report said the Midwest accounted for 41.7 percent of national demand, followed by 18 percent in the Central region and 15.6 percent in the Northeast. The South accounted for 13 percent and the West 11.7 percent, it said.

Export orders placed with U.S. machine tool makers totaled 318 units in February, up slightly from 316 units in January, the report said. But they rose sharply from 155 units ordered in February last year.

The latest figures were from the ninth U.S. Machine Tool Consumption report, which replaced monthly data on U.S. machine tool orders, shipments and exports issued by the Association for Manufacturing Technology.
Demand in the first two months of 1997 was estimated at $1.15 billion, up 13 percent from $1.01 billion in the first two months of last year.
